title: Getting Started
body:
Knowing you can break things down into smaller steps for any task you find overwhelming is really helpful!

Setting aside 25 minutes with the do not disturb sign on your phone, and quickly dealing with any interruptions like I’ll be 15 minutes we can talk then, 
Is much better than saying can’t you seeI’m busy  go away.?!!

Finding the space you feel really relaxed is important in making your commitment to a 25 minute time block, in my case, 
Quiet room with the sun shining in,trees & sky,around is perfect!










!
author: Babsbomber

title: Cancelled,$140 was still charged and will not respond to email
body: I had selected to cancel during the subscription and they still charged me a full year’s subscription of $140.  I have emailed the contact email address with no response to date.
author: Bean2378

title: excellent but horrendously expensive
body: 5 stars except for the price. i have gained a lot learning about myself and adopting strategies they suggest
author: Onetaste

title: All Hype - No Satisfaction
body:
This app is promoted as being a market leader in ADHD support and insight but fell short at the first interaction. 
Clunky interface, ridiculously expensive and not at all as it sells itself.
Difficult to use. Limited usability. Frustrating. 
My advice, keep looking….. my experience with the Liven app for the first time this evening was much easier to use, way more engaging and had a beneficial result from my first interaction.
author: ihasb Wilde

title: Recent Diagnosis
body: I recently got diagnosed with ADHD at 40. This app has been my personal assistant for learning, retraining my brain and comfort in anxious times. The AI Quinn has helped, I ask her questions, get help responding to texts that are difficult and even get advise for tricky work situations. The modules are quick bursts of education and so insightful. This app is so wonderful and comforting for the distress that comes with ADHD. Thank you
author: BDizzle1ful

title: Is this the only way to get a refund?
body: For a company that focuses on supporting ADHD you really don’t seem to care about good process. Trying to get a refund is IMPOSSIBLE. I signed up for Inflow over 12 months ago - paid for 12 months access, rarely used the app as didn’t find benefit, got a new phone, never logged back in. Fast forward to a few weeks ago when a $284 charge pops up in my card for Inflow. No prior comms/reminders on upcoming renewal (I’ve searched everywhere) just a big fat payment taken from my account. Great. Go hunting for how to contact/get a refund/cancel my account - not easy to find as not on the App, it’s on a website. Have to figure out login details etc. Finally work it all out - send email as instructed. No response. Send follow up. Still no response. Seriously. Come to the App Store to see if there are any other contact options - find out this appears to be a VERY common issue. Am now assuming this is your profit strategy. Seriously. Do better.
author: Ms_Becca_J

title: Shells
body: Love to short impactful bites of info and action . Communicating with Quin is brilliant
author: Shells🌻

title: Best app for add/adhd
body: Inflow has so many modules that help understand & manage better. It also has a great community forum section, which helps with not feeling alone with this. I think the focus body double sessions are good too (although a heads up for people outside the US - time difference elsewhere in the world makes attending these impossible, which is a huge downer). But I do use the app everyday, and overall, highly recommend it!🌟🌟
author: DearyMe!

title: Taking advantage of people
body:
This app promised a free trial and then a weekly subscription price. Once my free trial was over it charged $185.43 - the yearly price.
The app goes out of its way to be misleading. 
After reading through all the other reviews I can see this has been a problem for many people.
author: leteasha-may

title: Really helpful
body: I’m really liking this app and finding it really useful. really like the structure and the simple way each module is presented. I’m getting a lot of personalised tips from my chats with Quinn, this is a great feature.
author: SquaredEMC

title: Frustrating cancellation process & no support
body: I signed up hoping this would be a helpful ADHD tool, but canceling was a nightmare. Unlike most apps, you can’t cancel through the App Store directly — you have to go through their own system, which is confusing and not user-friendly. I tried to cancel and was still charged. I’ve sent multiple emails and haven’t received a single reply. For an app aimed at people with ADHD, the design feels especially unfair.
author: Me maybe you

title: Is this designed only for people who are medicated?
body: Not friendly for inattentive ADHD brains in the slightest… so much text and reading “homework” to do. Biggest waste of money ever, not user friendly for adhd. This is my first review I’ve left on the App Store in 14 years, so, I’m serious.
author: Amber Knight

title: Little by little
body: I found Inflow really helpful, in that it teaches you to look at why and how you are procrastinating( that is my main problem but they do focus on other similar mental health type issues). It then helps you to work on very small ways to change things around and is very encouraging as you go. It is a fantastic help, unfortunately I couldn’t continue on with it due to my financial situation but the lessons I DID do opened my eyes enormously! I would thoroughly recommend it to anyone to give it a try!
author: Lemon tears

title: Amazing
body: This app has changed my life! Each lesson is broken down into steps that are easy to follow and understand. It doesn’t just tell you what the strategies are, it gives examples of how they can be implemented. I love that the app lets you know it’s ok not to get it right every time straight away and that change takes time and that it’s ok to make a mistake. It even has activities to do with my partner so he can help me implement new strategies and changes to help them stick.
author: SallyLvB

title: Useless
body:
Terrible to use and waste of time. 

App is not user friendly and just regurgitates what you can already look up on the internet. 

Also doesn’t properly remind you to stop and will bill you and not give a refund. 

Awful app DO NOT USE!!!
author: Brdge

title: Impossible to get a return
body: Whilst the program itself is good, it is near impossible to get a return and to get a reply regarding any queries. Despite cancelling I am still finding attempted charges of $324 a year later :-(. Inflow, please get back to me with my refund and ensure my subscription is cancelled.
author: Londonmum71

title: So helpful
body: A great app, it has some excellent practical tools and information without feeling like you’re reading a novel.
author: Drewsh88

title: Basic info, but helpful for those who haven’t already done the research
body: The information in inflow is good, but I found I was already familiar with it and didn’t want to continue beyond my free trial. Unfortunately I didn’t get a reminder before my trial was up, but the inflow team was very helpful with helping me cancel and refunding what I’d paid (luckily I caught the card charge on the day it went out)
author: JolieJ

title: Dodgy
body:
I had to cancel my visa card literally 10 minutes ago - my 5-day free sub was up and i was willing to give this platform a crack to deal with my ADHD.

Had to call my bank as they suspended my card, where I learned that this company tried taking a $318 payment for whatever reason, was then forced to cancel my card and acquire a new one which lead to me having to re-establish my financial details with every subscription, every regular payment in my life. Such a vicious and deceivng company, the total annual amount of what i had intnded to subscribe to would have only amounted to $100-150. So, this company is bs, they are total scammers and i wouldn’t risk it if i were you. 

People  livng with mental health problems don’t need this kind of drama. On top of this, i couldn’t pay for a parking ticket because my card was blocked and i was in a tight situation where I had to park my car there without any payment method, and now I’ve received a parking fine for that.

Cheers for that you tossers.
author: Clay1917

title: DO NOT USE THIS APP
body:
DISGUSTING app that PREYS ON ADHD people. Reeling you in then Stealing money to the tune of 80 bucks a month from me which I didn’t agree to 
Cancelling it - good luck it seems
author: Hadenoughaussie

title: Worth taking a chance on
body: Was looking for something I didn’t know existed until I found it in this app, I can incrementally learn to understand myself better at my own pace. It’s structured in such a way that shows great insight into how an ADHD mind is affected differently and provides actionable tools which i’ve been able to use to alter my thinking for my own betterment. Too good for me to not leave a review and share my own experience
author: Chazwazza178

title: Inflow is the core resource and a very powerful habit for me.
body:
Inflow has proven to be a core resource for me as I learn to live with my ADHD. A diagnosis that continues to make me question who I am, how I got to where I am in life, and how the world works around me. Inflow’s structure with daily learning modules is steadily increasing my understanding of ADHD. It explains why I have endured such confusion and suffering throughout my life (I was diagnosed at 58!) Inflow provides me with strategies that I can actually understand, that I can logically accept and that I increasingly use in most aspects of my daily life. It hasn’t cured me (ha ha) but I do know more about why I do things the way I do. 
Amazingly I am still doing Inflow most every day, that is, for more than 2 months which is an achievement that only people with ADHD would appreciate. That’s a great achievement for me. The appbmust be structured just for us, and is rewarding enough for me to remain engaged and not to get distracted by something “shiny” elsewhere.  
The inflow app continues to be a crucial resource, for me, in my attempts to reduce the ADHD related suffering affecting me and those around me, my family and work mates .
Unexpectedly, there are other insights. For example I have also developed a degree of compassion for myself -both in the here and now, and also for myself in the past, as a child, a teenager, and throughout my adult life. I also increasingly understand why the people in my story responded the way they did. 
I strongly recommend investing in this program  to the people like myself who are genuinely confused and overwhelmed by their diagnosis that may have caused them to question everything that they thought they knew about themselves and the world around them.
In all honesty, I have to say that at first I was hesitant to start the app. Financially it was a big commitment. And would Ibstay the course?  However, based on my positive experience with the Additude website, combined with the usual overwhelming, in the moment, impulse to do the program, I swept this hesitation aside and pressed the “GET”  button. 
It costs me about about a $1 AUD a day. Much less than my mild online shopping habit and  I think it is well worth it. I do the modules-virtually every day-and has it has proved to be a rewarding and valuable part of my new routine.
Inflow has, I believe,  proven to be, for me, a significant, meaningful and positive new habit. It is a learning experience that is practical and applicable to my daily activities. It is as you might say “real world friendly” 

This is a genuine review- I am a real person. I am not being paid to write this. 

( although I wouldn’t turn down any little presents from George and the gang.)
author: Eddy Edface

title: One of the best tools out there
body: Not only it is packed with amazing lessons and hacks but also i kinda use it for emotional support , also when i am about to be sucked into doom scrolling i open inflow and complete a task
author: Atinathefirst

title: Taking advantage of people with ADHD
body: After deleting this app they continued to take large amounts of money each month. I asked for refund as I had not had the app for over 6 months and it wasn’t showing up in subscriptions. They said they could only refund 28 days which is ridiculous and over $600 to nothing. I think it’s really yucky businesses would operate this way quietly stealing your money. I had no idea I was paying for this. It feels more like a way to scam people with adhd then help them.
author: sunsarajewellery

title: well thought out app  , informative and needed
body: Although it is expensive, it is a well made app and very helpful
author: Sarahlarose

title: Charged after canceling subscription
body:
I will start by saying I did very much enjoy the free trial of this app although there is no way I can afford $314.45 AUD to use it as much as I would have loved to. 

I was very mindful of the cost (and my raging case of ADHD) so was sure to follow the specific instructions emailed to me on how to cancel my subscription. I very proudly did this with a couple of days until the trial ended and I was floored to see that my credit card had been charged the above amount this morning. 

I have emailed the team and am hoping for a quick resolution. 

Please be aware as I even double checked in my subscriptions that this was cancelled prior to the trial ending. (It is still showing cancelled so I have been invoiced but can’t even use the app)
author: kagam

title: Bravo Inflow
body:
I’m quite sceptical  about motivational apps pertaining  to ADHD, but this one seems like it’s been perfectly tailored for my brain. A pleasant surprise and a compelling program. 
Thanks.
author: Virginiaww

title: Scam
body: This app has charged my card multiple times even though I cancelled my subscription months ago. I have emailed them requesting a refund for these charges, if I do not hear back I will be taking further action.
author: Wayno1997

title: Beware of the payment trap
body:
I didn’t find this app particularly useful although I will not say it is bad just that it did not personally help me.
What is clear is that they will charge you USD$200 after 7 days of signing up which is insane. 
Luckily I ended my subscription immediately when I worked this out but I feel like it is not particularly transparent and also not very easy to work out how to do it.
Beware of the trap, they say they will refund it if you don’t like the app which is great but I wouldn’t risk it if I were you.
author: Ozza1984

title: Dodgy subscription model
body: The app promises that it is easy to cancel free subscription and that you can even get a refund if you miss the date (which adhd-ers are likely to do). However, I’ve been charged and it isn’t listed in my subscriptions in order for me to cancel. The instructions on the email are of no help. Feels like they’re taking advantage of adhd weaknesses
author: LJV1006

title: Trish
body: I do not recommend this product . I am trying to cancel my subscription and it hasn’t worked , very difficult to navigate .
author: Burchell142

title: Charged for 12 months after trial unable to cancel subscription
body:
I am really dissatisfied that I was charged for 12 months instead of being charged monthly, so therefore I can’t cancel any time.
It takes time to find out if an app is suitable to my needs
I am trying to submit my review and I have to enter a nick name, the app says my multiple attempts to choose a nickname are all taken. 
Convenient way to stop me leaving a negative review
author: Servakq

title: Scamware
body: Will ask you personal questions and only then reveal that they want $25 a month.
author: geekrebel

title: Pricing structure takes advantage of adhd
body:
The last thing I want to do is use adhd as an excuse for my short comings. I’m trying my best to manage my adhd. I don’t appreciate when an app that markets itself to help people with adhd takes advantage of the people it claims to help. 

I only used it two or three times while it was free. Usually on apple you can find what you’re subscribed to in the “manage subscription” somehow you cannot find inflow’s subscription even if you paid with Apple Pay. I absolutely should have been more careful. Because of this I’ve been put off inflow. 

For those who want an app that can help with adhd make sure you’re make sure you’re good at managing your emails. Inflow will send you promotional emails even after they charge you the full amount.
author: Velocityx101

title: Pretty Good
body:
I’d give this app four and a half stars, but it could be a five. 

This app is really good and is the best all rounder for ADHD in my opinion. Price is no issue when trying to better myself so that is not important in my opinion. But I do validate the reason for others.

My main feedback is to have a better locking system for the modules. This prevents someone like me, and I’m sure others from unlocking other tasks and modules in advance. Maybe the one week free trial is good for this exploration and I need some restraint for myself. But checking in each day and tasks being locked until the following day is a good idea as it gives you a goal or something to consider during that one day. For example, in the module with the launchpad, you could have the next days module locked so you can do it or at least think about it/have a creative solution like this. I know the app has a  “challenges” section and this is really good, but these should be imbedded within the module after the quiz. That way you can visually see it after completing the module and then it takes you to the challenges section when you click on it. 

I’m thinking of another app that does this well that I believe this app could benefit from. Just something to take into consideration with experimentation of the functions. However, overall this app has the best content which I’m happy with regardless. 

Good job.
author: Kovi_211

title: Good but expensive
body: I like the design but it is a bit too expensive after the 7 day trial.
author: BrainGamer2013

title: Great but expensive
body: Love the app and the ideas beind it but it’s way too expensive.
author: giggirl26

title: No complaints
body: Currently testing the free trial as I can’t afford the monthly payments, but you can apply for a reduced price or extended free trial. For those who can pay it 100% lives up to its claim, definitely built by ADHD people for ADHD people. So thorough and informative, it’s the holy grail app
author: hocosmith

title: Can’t cancel at all!
body:
So unimpressed. An app that preys on neurodivergent people, and rips them off. 

I started a free trial, but now I’ve had to move all my money out of my bank account as they are now trying to take money for a subscription I don’t want. Can I cancel said subscription? Nope! Essentially this is designed so are forced to at least pay them one months subscription. 

I’ve tried to follow their instructions to cancel but am unable to. It basically impossible to cancel. 

Why am I cancelling? My so called “coach”, hasn’t been bothered to read my notes properly. Doesn’t fill me confidence, and made me feel not so good. Waste of time, and my god I wish they’d stop trying to take my money.
author: Fjsjrsjakangf

title: Scam
body: App wasn’t for me. Tried to find out if I was signed up for a trial and couldn’t see anything in the app about it. Checked my apple subscriptions and nothing was there so I assumed I wasn’t subscribed. Couldn’t unsubscribe because it’s not even in my subscriptions. Deleted the app right away and still charged. Will be reporting to fair trading if I don’t get my money back. Ridiculous app model.
author: Je Isk

title: Very helpful
body: I’ve struggled with managing my emotions most of my life. Sometimes you don’t even realise some of the behaviours that you exhibit until they’re pointed out to you. Inflow helps with not only identifying these behaviours but using proven psychological techniques to help you understand and ultimately change your behaviour. The modules have taught me a lot and having a coach available to bounce ideas off and hold you accountable is a bonus. A paid for 1 year and it ended up costing me less than a 1 hour session with a therapist. Absolutely worth the money.
author: nathanf1987

title: Apple App Store is a scam!
body:
Apple is complicit in allowing companies to scam us, take our personal data before advising on costs or terms of service before offering all your information! Seems a tad illegal to me. 

Imagine going into a store and having to provide all this information before knowing the price and product when buying some bread.

Preying on people with ADHD is a joke. 
Nowhere can you find the billing and pricing information without being stuffed around by this app.

It might be good but from the reviews clearly is Neurodivergent people are here to help these companies profit.

Back to the drawing board!
author: darlingtrent

title: Money money money
body: Seems these days you can only get on top of things if you have a ridiculous amount of money. I get these things take some time and money to set up, but $30 a month (USD) PER PERSON? Really? I can’t wait for the day people realise how dumb this is and collectively put companies like this out of business.
author: PenguinFlea

title: Adult ADHD user experience
body:
I feel really optimistic about this app from what I’ve already experienced. 

If you are serious about managing aspects of tour ADHD then this is worth your time and money. 

I really enjoy how the learning is delivered - bite sized and easy to implement. Most importantly great ideas to help the new habit stick. After all ADHD people always have great ideas, just can’t remember what we were implementing the next day.

This is the real deal but those that will value this app will be People who are serious about wanting help and aren’t just looking for ‘cheap’ solutions. 

It’s a five star rating from me. Well done to the people behind it. And thank you for your passion and expertise that has gone into this.
author: Dani gb

title: The Best!
body: For years I’ve been looking for the ‘killer app’ for ADHD. I’ve found it. I use this daily and work with a real life human coach. It’s jam packed with good stuff. Great self and guided coaching, insights and more content than I think I could consume in a lifetime. So many apps are just along for the ride with the ADHD community: generalized apps marketing themselves to everybody including people with ADHD. But they are focused on ADHD. Inflow IS. It’s gold. Highly highly recommend it. A superb investment.
author: My Password Is

title: Billing issue resolved quickly
body: Had a billing issue related to free trial. This was resolved quickly and refund processed within a couple of days.
author: Rubbish crashes

title: Adult ADHDer
body:
Great app for adults with ADHD. Especially if you had a late diagnosis. 

Lots of resources. Coaching is great. Very comforting to be pet of a community.
author: Matt, Jo & Zoe

title: Saddened
body:
I was super happy with the app and I quite adored it. The price is absolutely ridiculous and unaffordable, I understand the work that goes into the app hence the price but it’s just the price is a huge deterrent towards the app and that is felt amongst many other people.

It would be so much more better to have a no payment plan option with limited usage of the app like many other apps instead of forcing me onto a plan which I can in no way afford!

What a shame, I really liked it.
author: anonymouscatapillar

title: Automatic payment system
body: Extremely inappropriate, exploitative, and predatory payment system specifically designed to trick people with ADHD and other mental disorders into spending money.
author: 1234realperson

title: No refund if you forget
body: Nowhere in your terms and conditions does it state a refund is available if the customer forgets. What is clearly stated though is that subscription payments made through the two most common app stores Apple’s APP STORE and Googles PLAYSTORE are final and non refundable. So I don’t like my chances of being refunded your subscription fee which is way too much by the way in any scenario. So the huge subscription fee and the deceiving refund claim made me delete the app before I even started. Disappointed
author: nick-626

title: The Carrot and The Stick
body:
The Carrot
Manage your ADHD in 5 minutes a day

The Stick
Too expensive without a decent look behind the curtain first, and by decent I mean longer than 7 days. I am the father of a family of 4, all of us have ADHD. It's crazy in my house and we all have different needs. I can't afford 4 accounts to keep us all sane. The numbers just don't stack up. Speaking of which is it $33/mth USD or AUD? I have no way of knowing? And if you multiply that by x4 it blows out to a massive USD $132/mth or AUD $185/mth for my family, either way NOT A CHANCE I would pay for either. Sorry.

This app could be useful, if I knew more about what it actually does up front. Give users a bigger carrot and you're more likely to get my money. I totally understand you have a team of BA's, QA's, Engineers, UX, UI etc to pay for but sadly your trial is too short and the price point is too high. I have deleted my account. 

So here's a User Story for you to take back to your team:
As a... parent and family with ADHD 
I want... a better opportunity to see the benefits of the app with affordable access 
So that... my family's ADHD can be managed better together

All the best
author: philberesford

title: Nope
body: Too expensive
author: vampireslayer14

title: Easy to use
body: I’ve only started using the app recently but the first thing that stood out is it is simple and quick to use. I have so much to do every day and so little energy and motivation to get them done and I thought this app would be another thing to add to the list. I’m excited to keep using it.
author: Caalra

title: ADHD Subscription Trap
body: It looks as though it’s had a lot of thought put in to it but I couldn’t even remember to use it during the free trial. I received the email about the free trial ending during work hours and forgot to unsubscribe after work. Really frustrating. I’d read somewhere on a review in here that they’re good about refunds if you forget to cancel (because ADHD) but since then I read through their policy and it says they won’t provide refunds. Now I’ve forked out over $100 that I can’t afford, for an app I won’t use. Aaargh! 🙈
author: Ange M N

title: Good app
body:
It’s a nice app which clearly has had a lot of thought put into it. I tried the preview and really liked the educative content, the community support aspect of it as well as the user interface. 

Although I agree that the app is of a quality for which I’d be happy to pay, I unfortunately  did have to cancel my subscription as I am a broke college student :( 

I was wondering if there were any discounts available for students? Until then I unfortunately won’t be able to benefit from this app (although I’d love to!) 

Thanks for the developers; keep up the good work!
author: MonkeyBrain318

title: Mindbogglingly expensive
body:
I’ve never seen an app with such an expensive ongoing cost and the idea of a 7-day trial after which you will be charged $30 automatically for the next month seems incredibly exploitative for a group who almost invariably struggle with the executive dysfunction that would make cancelling within those 7 days difficult. 

If you have ADHD and are not incredibly wealthy, don’t risk this.
author: Elevas

title: A fair price for the service provided
body:
This app is like headspace for headcases. Clearly a lot of love has gone into building this app and there seems to be a lot of clinical research backing it. As such I think it’s entirely fair for this to be a paid product. 

Another review said that the price was too high and that subscription services are an ADHD trap, yet one of the first things you see in the onboarding is “we will refund you if you forget to cancel”. Some people are rather ungrateful, and I can say I am grateful that the education around ADHD is improving, and I’m glad this service exists.
author: aewaewqwer

title: Way too expensive
body: Subscription apps are a real ADHD trap. Be mindful of your money before signing up.
author: GrapeTrousers
